clue.text: Go with many directors and face growth

parts.note: to go with someone in an argument is to side with them
a company's directors together form its boards

explanation.surface: Advice to join a crowd of company directors, then a jump to facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideboards are long side-whiskers grown down the cheeks, a British word for sideburns.

clue.text: Stands in boats

definitions.meaning: substitutes, players or people who take another's place

explanation.definitionFit: Short for substitutes and for submarines, the one word covers both stand-ins and underwater craft.

clue.text: Decline daughter — that is a method

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Someone says a daughter's decline is just her chosen method.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase, to fade away gradually, a sound or feeling growing weaker and ending.

clue.text: A doctor's patient approach

parts.note: patient reads as calm and tolerant, but also as the person being treated: how a doctor deals with those in the ward

explanation.surface: A description of a physician's calm and tolerant style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' works twice: the adjective meaning tolerant, and the noun for the person a doctor treats.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the manner and tact a physician shows towards people under their care.

clue.text: A cold greeting, always, for this person getting a goal!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hi is an informal greeting
ever, as in for ever, means always

explanation.surface: A chilly hello and a constant presence, all for someone who reaches their target.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reaches what they aim for is a person of accomplishment, a success.

clue.text: Slaver and doctor — gents that should be shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing a word up means it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, a loo in British slang

explanation.surface: A doctor's men's toilets ought to be exposed for being disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns LOO into OOL beneath DR. 'Slaver' is the verb to dribble, not a slave trader.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, a synonym for dribbling.

clue.text: Detailed description of glasses? Not quite!

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles, glasses

explanation.surface: Asking whether glasses count as a full description, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last S from SPECS.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, a detailed statement of requirements or features.

clue.text: Origin of Hamlet found amongst lost papers, possibly

indicators.note: found amongst places one letter inside the other letters
lost papers are muddled and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: The source of Shakespeare's play might be among some lost documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges PAPERS to PERAPS; 'found amongst' sets H, from 'Origin of Hamlet', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of uncertainty meaning maybe.

clue.text: Investor first to support Tokyo, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another is placed beneath it

parts.note: Tokyo is a capital city, the capital of Japan
first is written 1st, read as the letters IST

explanation.surface: An investor is the first to back a Japanese venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts IST (1st) under CAPITAL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into businesses for profit, a backer of enterprise.

clue.text: Extent of suspicion about Germany

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a breath of scandal is a hint or suspicion of it
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: How far mistrust of Germany reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BREATH round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Width or wide range, the full scope of something.

clue.text: Exposed rock group (banned) runs into policeman

parts.note: something banned is out, not allowed

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A banned rock band crosses paths with a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside COP to give CROP. 'rock group' looks like a band, but it is a cluster of exposed stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock that pokes up through the surface soil.

clue.text: Silly bet — let in a chap to be the deciding factor

indicators.note: a silly arrangement is a jumbled one, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A foolish wager: allow some fellow in and he will settle matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' signals rearranging BET LET IN A CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to swing an outcome one way, like extra weight tilting a pair of scales.

clue.text: Wheel patient being treated outside hospital — a useless and expensive thing

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping round a further letter
treating something changes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Wheeling a patient out of hospital for treatment proves costly and pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being treated' signals the anagram and 'outside' wraps it round the hospital letter. 'patient' reads as a person in a ward, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Siamese kings' costly gift of a sacred albino beast, means a burdensome possession.

clue.text: European broadcast on aim for border crossing

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a Czech is a European, from the Czech Republic
to point something is to aim it

explanation.surface: A European radio programme about aiming for the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' gives CHECK, which sounds like CZECH.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded barrier at a frontier where travellers and their papers are inspected.

clue.text: Sniffy reaction for Coward's work?

definitions.meaning: an allergy to pollen that sets the nose running and sniffing
a 1925 comedy by the English playwright Noël Coward

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is the playwright Noël Coward, not a timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen allergy shares its name with Noël Coward's comic play about a bohemian family.

clue.text: Tool the man's smuggled into prison finally going missing

indicators.note: smuggled into means slipped inside
the final letter of the word goes missing, dropped from the end

parts.note: a prison cell
his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: A man's implement is sneaked into a jail, though it's lost in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally going missing' trims the jail word to CEL before 'smuggled into' puts the possessive inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade with a bevelled edge used for cutting wood or stone, a hand tool.

clue.text: Permit amorous advance after drink? On the contrary

indicators.note: after would place the pass beneath the drink, but the clue then reverses that

parts.note: to make a pass is to make an amorous advance
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A romantic move made after a drink, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' overturns 'after', so the advance comes first and the drink second.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is official permission to leave and enter countries.

clue.text: A tax credit having priority for some menswear?

indicators.note: having priority means coming first, so this piece goes to the front

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: Could a tax break be a priority when buying men's clothes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'having priority' moves the credit abbreviation in front. Value added tax is Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckerchief tied like a broad scarf, worn by men in place of a tie.

clue.text: Poor lamb, say? Poor indeed

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so these letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a lamb, then a harsh verdict on the meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Poor' signals rearranging LAMB SAY; the second is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful, extremely bad: very poor in quality.

clue.text: Zones where football supporters are put in coolers?

definitions.text: Zones where football supporters are put in coolers?

parts.words: Zones where football supporters are put in coolers?
parts.note: areas of fans in a stadium, and also the engine parts driving a car's radiator fan

explanation.surface: Where football supporters are corralled into chilled enclosures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a stadium zone for fans, but the parts are found in a car's cooling system.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber loops in a car engine that drive the radiator fan, part of the cooling system.

clue.text: Stipulate deposit — and put one's cards on the table?

definitions.meaning: to ... rules is to stipulate them
to place something down, to set it on a surface

definitions.text: put one's cards on the table
definitions.meaning: in card games, to show one's hand by placing it face up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers setting rules, putting something on a surface, and revealing a hand of cards.

clue.text: Did, say, apply an innovative parking scheme

indicators.note: an innovative version is a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a council adopted a new parking system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innovative' signals the rearrangement of DID SAY APPLY AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A car park system where drivers buy a ticket and leave it on show in the windscreen.

clue.text: Food store outside hotel in city

indicators.note: outside means wrapping round another letter

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A delicatessen standing beside a hotel in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts DELI round H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital region is an example of a city.

clue.text: Blubber about student accommodation

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: blubber is whale fat
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone is going on about student housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like the verb to sob; it is fat. 'about' puts FAT round L.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment, a set of rooms to live in, is a form of housing.

clue.text: One exam covering 2,000 — that's wrong!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for 1,000, so two of them make 2,000
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A single test spanning two millennia — outrageous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' has the exam wrap round the two Roman thousands.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally bad, against accepted standards of right conduct.

clue.text: Have objective that's self-defeating?

definitions.note: the definition describes a thing: something that works against one's own interests

parts.note: to own something is to have it
an objective is a goal, an aim

explanation.surface: Asking whether having an aim might be counterproductive.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a goal scored into one's own net gives points to the opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an act that harms one's own cause, from football's goal scored against one's side.

clue.text: Spill the beans and count

definitions.meaning: to reveal a secret, to inform
to count, as a bank teller counts money or voters are counted

explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to reveal a secret and, in older use, to number or reckon up.

clue.text: Make a granny get married

definitions.meaning: a granny is a kind of knot, so making one means tying it
to wed, to become husband and wife

explanation.walkthrough: A granny is not a grandmother here but a simple, slip-prone knot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to marry, and literally describes forming a knot such as a granny.
